title: Pin the required release-drift renderer to the exact build represented by committed exports
decision_statement: Declare SRS_RUST_CLI_TAG exactly once in the release-drift workflow, pin it to v0.1.0-build.265, make the required check download that exact renderer, log its tag and checksum, and require any future pin advance and corresponding documentation re-render to land together as one reviewable change.

sources.excerpt: The workflow explains that an unpinned required gate can change without an SRS commit, declares SRS_RUST_CLI_TAG once as v0.1.0-build.265, and defines advancing the pin and re-rendering as two halves of one fact that must land together.
The required job downloads the release named by SRS_RUST_CLI_TAG, logs that tag and the binary SHA-256, then runs release drift with SRS_CLI_PATH bound to the downloaded binary.

Merged 2026-08-01T22:15:50Z. The PR reports that the same records fail release drift with build.263 and pass with build.265, which is the first release carrying RFC-037's renderer; committed docs/spec output was deliberately left unchanged.

Issue #316 identifies the defect: release-drift was required but downloaded the latest cross-repository binary, so its behavior changed without any commit and produced failures indistinguishable from genuine record drift.

alternatives: Continue downloading the latest srs-rust release so the gate stays automatically fresh.
Treat v0.1.0-build.265 as a minimum and permit any newer release.
Pin the tag separately in each consuming step or helper.
Re-render committed exports whenever an unpinned required check begins failing.
accepted_cost: The required gate intentionally stops receiving renderer updates automatically; maintainers must review a pin bump and any resulting export or mirror changes together, and contributors must use the exact named build rather than whichever srs binary is locally current.
supersedes: release-drift latest-release download without a tag
derived_from: RFC-037 renderer changes first released in v0.1.0-build.265
Epic-256 requirement that generated artifacts have an auditable chain

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Resolving the latest renderer is operationally convenient and automatically fresh, but it can report committed semantic sources as stale when only an external executable changed.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The workflow keeps the exact renderer easy to fetch from one declared tag and documents a four-step procedure for advancing it.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A reproducibility pin has over-rotated when it blocks a deliberate renderer upgrade after the outputs, mirrors, and reason for the upgrade are ready to be reviewed together.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Following every new srs-rust release evolves the gate immediately, but makes required-check behavior change outside this repository's versioned decision history.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Evolution remains explicit: update the single pin and regenerate with that exact build in the same PR; a no-diff verified bump is allowed.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Continuity has become inertia if the pin remains old after a newer renderer has been intentionally selected and its complete projection delta can be reviewed.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Allowing CI and each contributor to use their locally available renderer reduces setup friction but permits the same records to produce different results across environments.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The renderer identity has one declaration, the fetch path is automated, and provenance is logged so local and CI failures can be attributed without central guesswork.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Central coherence has overreached if unrelated tools that deliberately track latest releases are pinned without evidence that their output participates in this required artifact chain.

coding_notes: Independent Pass-A supplemental coding of the release-renderer pin. The decision is counted as reasoned application rather than mechanical derivation because the chosen equality policy, single source of truth, exact build, coupled advancement procedure, and deliberate exclusion of unrelated latest-tracking workflows encode explicit tradeoffs. The implementation is delivered at merge commit c132784ce959787b5ee40b2472c4b996abe35363.
